projection: equirectangular (plate carree, EPSG:4326); texture and DEM cover the bbox edge to edge

texture.note: grayscale luminance; u=0 is the bbox west edge, v=0 the north edge (image top = north)

dem.order: row-major, north row first, Int16 LE
dem.registration: node (i,j) is at lon = west + i*(east-west)/(w-1), lat = north - j*(north-south)/(h-1); so node 0 sits on the west/north bbox edge and node w-1 / h-1 on the east/south edge
dem.note: each node is the mean of the source (zoom-9, ~280 m) pixels inside its cell, sea and negative values clamped to 0 before averaging; coastal land below ~1 m is also 0. Averaging smooths peaks: the raw 280 m maximum in the bbox is 2980 m.

sources.name: NASA GIBS WMTS, VIIRS Suomi/NOAA-21 corrected reflectance true colour
sources.licence: NASA EOSDIS data use policy: freely accessible; unless a restriction is marked, NASA-led mission data are CC0; acknowledgement of NASA GIBS requested
sources.layer_or_dataset: VIIRS_NOAA21_CorrectedReflectance_TrueColor, tile matrix set 250m, zoom 8, 15 daily scenes 2026-10-18 to 2026-11-15 every 2 days
sources.note: per-pixel 40th-percentile luminance across the dates (removes cloud, dust, sun glint, swath gaps), cropped to the bbox, downsampled to 1536 px, tone-curved, grayscale. The WELD Landsat 30 m layer named in the brief was NOT used: its imagery ends in 2000, before Palm Jumeirah, The World, Saadiyat or most of the current coast existed.

sources.name: AWS Open Data: Terrain Tiles (Mapzen / Tilezen joerd), terrarium encoding
sources.licence: Mixed public-domain and open sources. In this bbox: SRTM (public domain, USGS credit requested) on land and ETOPO1 (NOAA, public domain) for sea, GMTED2010 (USGS, no restrictions) at low zooms. No key, no account.
sources.note: height = R*256 + G + B/256 - 32768 m; area-averaged to a 128x101 lon/lat grid, sea clamped to 0. AWS registry: https://registry.opendata.aws/terrain-tiles/

attribution: Imagery: NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), VIIRS NOAA-21. Terrain: SRTM and GMTED2010 courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey, ETOPO1 NOAA, via AWS Terrain Tiles.
